summary: Nepal grants a visa on arrival to almost every nationality — 30 USD for 15 days, 50 USD for 30 days or 125 USD for 90 days, all multiple entry and extendable — while Indian citizens cross the open border freely without a visa. An optional online form speeds up the arrival line.

travelInsurance.text: Border officers may ask to see a travel insurance document covering healthcare costs, repatriation and other emergencies in Nepal, along with confirmation of where you will spend your first night. Nepal's Department of Immigration does not list insurance among its visa-on-arrival steps (online form, fee receipt, passport), so this rests on the UK government's advice. For trekking, choose a policy that covers your maximum altitude and helicopter evacuation: a rescue flight can cost thousands of dollars.

currencyLimits.text: Travelers entering Nepal by air or land may bring foreign currency or travelers' cheques worth up to USD 5,000; anything above that must be declared at customs on arrival, and goods carried undeclared can be confiscated. No official source we could read states the current rules on carrying Nepali or Indian rupee notes, so check with your bank before carrying Indian 200- and 500-rupee notes.

notes: The UK FCDO says some skincare products and e-cigarette refills contain ingredients that are illegal in Nepal, such as CBD; police may seize them and charge you with drug possession.
The UK FCDO says it is illegal to buy, sell, kill or capture any wild animal or trade its parts without a licence, and that Nepal bans trade in wildlife products without a CITES permit.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says Nepal's economy is largely cash-based, though credit cards can be used in major stores, hotels and restaurants and ATMs are available in larger cities such as Kathmandu and Pokhara. The UK FCDO says ATMs are not reliable outside the main tourist sites and that remote areas may have neither ATMs nor card acceptance.

safety.text: Nepal is generally safe and welcoming, with petty theft the main urban risk. The real hazards are environmental: altitude sickness, mountain weather, road conditions and occasional strikes (bandhs) that halt transport. Flash floods in August 2026 badly damaged roads and buildings in Rasuwa district and along the Nepal–China border, and the authorities warn of further floods and landslides there.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says you need a valid permit and a TIMS (Trekking Information Management System) card to enter Nepal's main trekking regions, and that all foreign independent trekkers must use a local guide or porter in national parks and protected areas.

The UK FCDO advises making sure your insurance covers mountain rescue and helicopter costs, and warns that rapid helicopter evacuation can be hard to get in remote areas. It also reports guides taking trekkers too high too fast and then calling in helicopter evacuations they profit from.

The UK FCDO says you can apply online for a visa on arrival up to 15 days before you arrive, then collect and pay at the airport. You can pay by card, but bring cash as a back-up — US dollars are preferred.
Overstaying costs 3 USD per day plus fines and can mean being barred from future entry — extend at the Department of Immigration in Kathmandu or Pokhara before your visa runs out.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Nepal?
faq.answer: Yes, but it is issued on arrival: US passport holders (like almost all nationalities) get a tourist visa at Kathmandu airport or any land border — 30 USD for 15 days, 50 USD for 30 days or 125 USD for 90 days, multiple entry. Bring the fee in cash.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Nepal?
faq.answer: No. Under the 1950 India–Nepal friendship treaty the border is open: Indian citizens enter without a visa and without stay limits, using a passport or accepted identity document (airlines require a passport, voter ID or other approved ID for flights).

faq.question: How does Nepal's visa on arrival work?
faq.answer: On arrival you complete a form (or bring the receipt from the free online form at nepaliport.immigration.gov.np, submitted within 15 days before travel), pay the fee in cash and receive the visa sticker. Queues at Kathmandu airport can be long — the pre-filled form and exact cash speed things up.

faq.question: Can I extend my Nepal tourist visa?
faq.answer: Yes, at the Department of Immigration in Kathmandu or Pokhara: minimum 45 USD for 15 days, then 3 USD per day, up to a maximum of 150 days in Nepal per calendar year.

faq.question: Do I need permits for trekking in Nepal besides the visa?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK FCDO says you need a valid permit and a TIMS card to enter Nepal's main trekking regions, and that all foreign independent trekkers must use a local guide or porter in national parks and protected areas. It points to the Nepal Tourism Board for the TIMS requirements.
